title: Reed-Sternberg Cells, CD15 and CD30, and Classical Hodgkin Subtypes

steps.tx: The morphological hallmark of classical Hodgkin lymphoma is the **Reed-Sternberg cell**, an extraordinarily large binucleated or bilobed giant cell measuring twenty to fifty micrometers across. Under light microscopy, each nuclear lobe contains a prominent, inclusion-like, eosinophilic nucleolus surrounded by a clear halo of pale nucleoplasm, producing a pathognomonic owl-eye appearance. Although Reed-Sternberg cells represent the sole neoplastic element derived from crippled post-germinal centre B-cells, they characteristically constitute less than five percent of total cellularity in involved lymph nodes.
steps.say: The diagnostic hallmark of classical Hodgkin lymphoma is the binucleated Reed-Sternberg cell. Measuring up to fifty micrometers, each mirror-image nuclear lobe houses a massive, eosinophilic nucleolus that imparts a classic owl-eye appearance. Despite being the true clonal malignancy derived from mutated germinal center B-cells, Reed-Sternberg cells typically make up less than five percent of the tumor mass, being surrounded by an extensive reactive inflammatory infiltrate.

vis.alt: Micrograph of classical Reed-Sternberg cell with bilobed nucleus and large eosinophilic nucleoli
vis.caption: Reed-Sternberg pathology in classical Hodgkin lymphoma with reactive background.

steps.tx: Immunohistochemical profiling conclusively distinguishes classical Reed-Sternberg cells from non-Hodgkin lymphomas and reactive immunoblastic proliferations. Classical Reed-Sternberg cells consistently express **cluster of differentiation 30**, an activation marker displaying membrane and Golgi pattern staining, and CD15 (Leu-M1) in eighty-five percent of cases. Crucially, neoplastic cells downregulate typical B-cell antigens, demonstrating dim or absent PAX5 expression, complete absence of surface immunoglobulin, negative CD45 (leukocyte common antigen), and infrequent, weak staining for CD20.
steps.say: Immunohistochemistry is essential to confirm the diagnosis of classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Neoplastic Reed-Sternberg cells demonstrate strong positivity for CD30 with Golgi accentuation and express CD15 in the majority of cases. Importantly, they downregulate their original B-cell machinery, testing completely negative for CD45, lacking surface immunoglobulins, and showing only faint, attenuated expression of the transcription factor PAX5.

left.title: Classical Reed-Sternberg Profile
points: CD15 positive in 80% to 85% of cases
PAX5 dim positive; CD20 mostly negative

steps.tx: Accounting for seventy percent of classical Hodgkin cases in developed nations, **nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma** predominantly strikes adolescents and young adults between fifteen and thirty-four years of age, with a slight female predilection. Histologically, broad collagenous collagen bands divide the lymphoid parenchyma into circumscribed cellular nodules. The diagnostic variant cell is the lacunar cell, a Reed-Sternberg variant featuring folded, hyperlobated nuclei set within delicate cytoplasm that shrinks into empty artefactual spaces during formal fixation.
steps.say: Nodular sclerosis is the most common classical subtype, typically presenting in young adult females with painless supradiaphragmatic and mediastinal adenopathy. Collagen bands originate from the lymph node capsule to carve the tissue into distinct round nodules. The microscopic hallmark is the lacunar Reed-Sternberg cell, whose abundant cytoplasm contracts during formalin processing to leave a prominent clear space or lacuna around the folded nucleus.

vis.alt: Histological section of nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma showing fibrous collagen bands and lacunar cells
vis.caption: Hodgkin lymphoma Reed-Sternberg cells and staging framework.

steps.tx: Representing twenty to twenty-five percent of classical cases, **mixed cellularity classical Hodgkin lymphoma** displays a biphasic age distribution, peaking in young children in developing countries and adults over fifty years of age, with male predominance. Histologically, classic diagnostic Reed-Sternberg cells abound within a highly heterogeneous inflammatory background rich in small lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells, and epithelioid histiocytes. Eosinophil recruitment is driven by tumour-secreted interleukin-5. More than seventy percent of mixed cellularity cases harbour clonal Epstein-Barr virus.
steps.say: Mixed cellularity accounts for nearly a quarter of classical Hodgkin lymphomas and shows a strong male predominance. The background is a rich cellular mixture of mature lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, and abundant eosinophils attracted by tumor-derived interleukin-5. Unlike nodular sclerosis, collagen bands are absent, diagnostic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells are easily found, and over seventy percent of cases demonstrate clonal Epstein-Barr virus integration.

steps.tx: Accounting for approximately five percent of classical cases, **lymphocyte-rich classical Hodgkin lymphoma** presents primarily in middle-aged males with localized peripheral lymphadenopathy. Microscopic examination demonstrates scattered classic diagnostic Reed-Sternberg cells situated within expansive nodules or sheets composed almost entirely of mature small lymphocytes, lacking the neutrophilic or eosinophilic background of mixed cellularity. It must be carefully differentiated from nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma by demonstrating positive CD30 and CD15 staining on neoplastic cells, carrying an excellent long-term prognosis.
steps.say: Lymphocyte-rich classical Hodgkin lymphoma represents about five percent of classical cases and usually presents as localized, early-stage peripheral lymphadenopathy in middle-aged men. Under the microscope, classic Reed-Sternberg cells are nestled within a sea of mature small lymphocytes, with virtually no eosinophils or fibrosis. Demonstrating CD30 and CD15 positivity confirms its classical nature and prevents misdiagnosis as non-classical nodular lymphocyte predominant disease.

right.title: Nodular Lymphocyte Predominant
points: Often managed with rituximab or local radiation

steps.tx: Establishing a definitive histological diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma mandates an **excisional lymph node biopsy** rather than fine-needle aspiration cytology or core-needle sampling. Because diagnostic Reed-Sternberg cells comprise less than five percent of total tissue volume, fine-needle aspiration frequently samples only reactive background lymphocytes, resulting in false-negative interpretations. An intact excisional biopsy preserves architectural topography, allowing pathologists to evaluate capsular thickening, collagen banding, nodular versus diffuse compartmentation, and spatial relationships between neoplastic cells and the inflammatory infiltrate.
steps.say: Excisional lymph node biopsy remains the gold standard for diagnosing Hodgkin lymphoma. Fine-needle aspiration cytology is notoriously inadequate and should never be used to establish a primary diagnosis, because Reed-Sternberg cells make up only a tiny fraction of the cellularity and are easily missed. Intact tissue architecture is mandatory to assess capsular fibrosis, identify collagen bands, and confirm classical immunophenotypic staining within the intact microenvironment.

steps.tx: Prognostication in advanced-stage classical Hodgkin lymphoma relies on the **International Prognostic Score**, which evaluates seven independent baseline clinical and laboratory adverse risk factors. Each factor scores one point: male sex, age forty-five years or older, Stage IV disease, serum albumin under four grams per deciliter, haemoglobin under 10.5 grams per deciliter, leukocytosis exceeding fifteen thousand per microliter, and absolute lymphocytopenia under six hundred per microliter or eight percent of total white cells.
steps.say: The International Prognostic Score stratifies risk in advanced stage three and four Hodgkin lymphoma using seven independent adverse variables. Clinicians award one point each for male sex, age forty-five or older, stage four disease, albumin below four, haemoglobin below ten point five, white cell count above fifteen thousand, and absolute lymphocyte count below six hundred. Patients with five or more points face significantly lower five-year progression-free survival.

steps.tx: Due to curability rates exceeding eighty-five percent with modern anthracycline chemotherapy and involved-site radiotherapy, **long-term treatment survivorship** represents a central management concern. Late complications emerge one to three decades following cure, dominated by secondary solid malignancies including female breast carcinoma and lung cancer developing within previous radiation fields, alongside accelerated coronary artery disease and anthracycline-induced dilated cardiomyopathy. Screening mammography and annual cardiovascular surveillance are essential lifelong commitments.
steps.say: Because over eighty-five percent of Hodgkin lymphoma patients achieve long-term cure, minimizing late therapeutic toxicity is paramount. Survivors face significant risks decades after treatment, including radiation-induced breast and lung cancers, secondary acute myeloid leukaemia from alkylating agents, and accelerated coronary artery stenosis. Modern protocols use involved-site radiation and lower anthracycline doses, backed by structured lifelong screening including early annual mammography for irradiated females.

left.title: Malignant Late Toxicity
points: Breast cancer in irradiated young women

quiz.q: Which histological variant of the Reed-Sternberg cell is pathognomonic of nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma?
options: Lacunar cell with retracted delicate cytoplasm
Popcorn cell with folded multilobed nucleus
Pleomorphic giant cell with bizarre polyploidy
quiz.explain: Lacunar cells are characteristic Reed-Sternberg variants seen in nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma, showing artifactual cytoplasmic shrinkage creating a clear lacuna around the nucleus.

quiz.q: Which immunohistochemical staining pattern definitively characterizes neoplastic cells in classical Hodgkin lymphoma?
options: CD15 positive, CD30 positive, CD45 negative
CD20 bright positive, CD45 positive, CD15 negative
CD3 positive, CD5 positive, CD30 negative
CD10 positive, BCL6 positive, CD15 negative
quiz.explain: Classical Reed-Sternberg cells consistently express CD30 and usually CD15, while lacking leukocyte common antigen CD45 and typical B-cell antigens like bright CD20.

quiz.q: What is the primary reason why fine-needle aspiration (FNA) is inadequate for diagnosing Hodgkin lymphoma?
options: Reed-Sternberg cells make up less than 5% of tissue cellularity amidst reactive cells
Needle puncture consistently triggers tumor lysis syndrome
Flow cytometry cannot detect cluster of differentiation antigens on needle washes
Eosinophils present in the node neutralize immunohistochemical antibodies
quiz.explain: Neoplastic Reed-Sternberg cells represent under 5% of cells in involved nodes; FNA frequently samples only the reactive inflammatory milieu, resulting in high false-negative rates.
